text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a skin lesion on your chest; can you tell me how long it has been there and if it has changed in size, color, or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Basal Cell Carcinoma

Given the 63-year-old male's age, two-month history of a growing chest lesion, and lack of symptoms, this presentation is highly suspicious for Basal Cell Carcinoma, which is more common on sun-exposed areas. I will now request a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy of chest lesion.
